# NOSOCOMIAL PNEUMONIA WITH STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS

# Methicillin-SUSCEPTIBLE Staphylococcus aureus pneumonia (mec-A/C and MREJ not detected)

Duration of therapy 7 days

Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h R

---

References:

- Liu C, Clin Infect Dis. 2011:52:285
- Wunderink RG, Clin Infect Dis. 2012: 54:621
- Rybak MJ, Clin Infect 2009: Dis 49:325
- Sanford Keyword: Staphylococcus aureus pneumonia John Hopkins Antimicrobial
- Guide www.johnhopkinsguides.com
Therapy:
## Oral therapy (usually given after several days of intravenous therapy):

A patient who is substantially improved, without a fever for at least 2 days can be treated with an oral agent to which the isolate is susceptible.

Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h R

< OR >

Cephalexin 500 mg PO q6h ($) [R]

## Methicillin-RESISTANT or Susceptibilities Unknown Staphylococcus aureus (mec-A/C and MREJ detected)

In patients with MRSA pneumonia complicated by empyema, antimicrobial therapy should be used in conjunction with drainage procedures.

Duration of therapy 7 days.

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R

## Oral therapy (usually given after several days of intravenous therapy:

In cases when a patient has substantially improved and has not had a fever for at least 2 days, it may be appropriate to treat with an oral agent to which the isolate is susceptible to complete therapy.

Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI]

< OR >

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h R,DI
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU ABX NOSOCOMIAL STAPHYLOCOCCUS PNEUMONIA
